description: Δ_λ OPTION C — Demazure-fiber selector for the H_{3A} Wedderburn refinement of ρ_K (deuteron).  Replaces the Occam single-partition heuristic of rho_k_h3a_refinement.py with the derived rule Δ_λ ≡ y_λ(q_0) · D_w(λ)/D_{w_0}(λ) where D_w(λ) is the Demazure character at the canonical reduced word w of the underlying S_6 permutation π_β of the deuteron braid β_D, and D_{w_0}(λ) is the Demazure character at the longest element w_0 ∈ S_6.  This is the Demazure-fiber Markov-trace functional T^Dem from prop:demazure-fiber-markov-trace (commit e77a4b4d).  Reports the implied mass-equation closure residual.
engine: χ^λ via mpmath numeric Hoefsmit at q_0 (50 dps), multiprocessing.Pool(4); D_w via sympy Demazure operators at principal specialisation x_i ↦ q^{i−1}, evaluated at q_0 to 50 dps

parameters.braid_word_str: β_p · I · β_n  (canonical: H_3 ⊗ H_3 ⊂ H_6 with interface I = σ_3 - h/2·1 at gen_idx=2)

audit_reference: AUDIT-DEEP-2026-05.md §7 P3' — Δ_λ derivation race (Option C)
notes: Option C of the Δ_λ derivation race (PR #600 parent). The Demazure-fiber rule is a STRUCTURAL prediction: Δ_λ is fixed by the geometry of the braid (via π_β and D_w) and the Wenzl-bridge weight y_λ.  No tuning, no per-λ sign flips — the only free choice is the Coxeter projection π : B_n → S_n itself.  The closure error is the falsification signal: a value close to zero would validate the Demazure-fiber selector; a value at the MeV scale or larger means the rule is incomplete (e.g. missing a Hochschild-cohomology phase, or needs a different Coxeter section).  HONEST REPORTING: the outcome_classification field reports the verdict.
follow_up: If the closure passes, extend to (T, ³He) at n=9 and ⁴He at n=12 — the same code path applies (just longer Coxeter projection and bigger Demazure tables).  If the closure fails, sweep alternative reduced-word choices (every reduced word for the same π_β gives the SAME Demazure character — the operators satisfy the braid relations on reduced words — so this control is null).  Then sweep alternative Coxeter projections (e.g. signed lifts of σ_i⁻¹ that flip the underlying reflection).
